turns.user: Under the Arms Act, 1878, which section empowers the Government to establish searching posts along the country's border?

gold.answer: Section 11 of the Arms Act, 1878 empowers the Federal Government to establish searching-posts along the boundary-line between Pakistan and foreign territory, where vessels, carts, baggage-animals and packages in transit may be stopped and searched for arms, ammunition and military stores.

turns.user: Under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, apart from the mortgagor, who else can sue to redeem a mortgaged property?

gold.answer: Under section 91 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, besides the mortgagor, redemption may be sought by any person (other than the mortgagee) with an interest in or charge upon the property or the right to redeem, any surety for the mortgage-debt, and any creditor of the mortgagor who has obtained a decree for sale of the mortgaged property in a suit for administration of his estate.

evidence.quote: any person (other than the mortgagee of the interest sought to be redeemed) who has any interest in, or charge upon, the property mortgaged
any surety for the payment of the mortgage
any creditor of the mortgagor who has in a suit for the administration of his estate obtained a decree for sale of the mortgaged property

turns.user: My father is old and ill. He always said his plot in Karachi was meant for my sister, but my brother, who manages all his money and affairs, kept pressuring him until he signed the plot over to my brother instead.

We have not decided whether to go to court.
Based on what I told you at the start, what is the legal term for what my brother did to my father, and which section of the law defines it?

gold.answer: Section 16 of the Contract Act, 1872 defines undue influence: a person in a position to dominate another's will (for example, one who holds real or apparent authority over him or stands in a fiduciary relation to him, or deals with someone whose mental capacity is affected by age or illness) uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage.

evidence.quote: where the relations subsisting between the parties are such that one of the parties is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain an unfair advantage over the other
where he makes a contract with a person whose mental capacity is temporarily or permanently affected by reason of age, illness, or mental or bodily distress

turns.user: For the past month someone has been slipping unsigned letters under my shop door, threatening to burn my shop down unless I close it. I have no idea who is writing them.

I have not told my family yet.
My sister's wedding is next month and I am busy with preparations.
Going back to what I told you at the start, which section of the law deals specifically with the fact that the threats are unsigned, and how much extra imprisonment can it add?

gold.answer: Section 507 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 covers criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or where the person making the threat has taken precautions to conceal their name or abode. It adds imprisonment of either description for up to two years on top of the punishment for criminal intimidation under the preceding section.
